authorization: Owner 2026-11-08 (Toronto ~10:00): "按你的方法训练" — train with the method proposed after the human-endgame audit (section 67): solver-labelled self-play endgames, human endgames used only as a held-out test.
purpose: Mac-only solver-labelled endgame training: champion plays to the endgame, every candidate of each endgame decision is labelled with its exact perfect-information value averaged over worlds sampled from the mover's public information (PIMC), and a student initialised as the champion regresses these values. Research experiment; not a web release.
start: Exact copy of champion 017 (the oracle projection exists in the learner but its input is always zero: oracleDecaySteps 0); fresh Adam; empty replay; steps count from 0.
target: For each real endgame decision (table <= 20 cards, not a finishing move, >= 2 candidates) and EVERY candidate a: Q(s,a) = mean over 8 worlds (uniform deals of the unseen cards consistent with own hand, cards played and hand counts; sampleWorlds) of the exact perfect-information team-minimax value of a, in the mover team's signed single-round points (+-1/+-2/+-3, so avoiding a double-down counts). Worlds over budget are dropped; a decision needs >= 4 solved worlds or it is not recorded. No tempo, trick-control, bomb or partner proxy in reward, loss, gate or acceptance. The real hidden hands are used only for a descriptive diagnostic, never for a label.
approximation: PIMC is an approximation of the round value for a player who sees only their own hand: the uniform belief ignores what earlier plays reveal, and averaging perfect-information values overrates information learned only later (strategy fusion).

developmentEvidence.note: Measured before registration on development seeds (section-57 smoke block 3,838,0xx,xxx), not on held-out or human data.
developmentEvidence.labelQuality: 160 champion self-play rounds, 390 critical decisions at <= 20 cards (some move loses value in the real deal): label-best move truly optimal 91.8% (8 worlds) / 93.4% (16 worlds) vs champion 75.9%; mean true regret 0.12 / 0.10 vs 0.30 points.
developmentEvidence.throughput: 8 worlds at <= 20 cards: ~13 rows/s per actor (6-min pipeline smoke, 2 actors, 1,481 decisions, 0 skipped); <= 24 cards was ~9x slower, so the threshold is 20.
developmentEvidence.smoke: Supervisor + 2 PIMC actors + MPS learner, 6 minutes: 350 updates, exports e00000200/e00000350, loss EMA 0.34; smoke run discarded.

actor.note: Above 20 cards every seat plays champion greedy. At a labelled decision the next move is the label's best move with probability 0.5, else softmax(champion Q / 0.05).

seeds.scope: Audit read 478 locally readable evidence files, 133166 known roots; other machines' unpublished history is unverified.

stop: Fixed 10-hour deadline from first start; restarts use only the remaining time; STOP stops all processes; no extension; the owner may stop early.

evaluation.object: The final exported student at stop (models/latest.json), not an intermediate or best-looking export.
evaluation.primary: 3,000 held-out deals each played twice with sides swapped (6,000 single rounds): focal team plays champion until the table has <= 20 cards, then the student, greedy; the other team plays champion 017 throughout (evaluate.mjs --threshold=20). Metric: focal team's mean signed round points per deal pair with a 95% deal-cluster normal interval. Positive evidence only if the lower bound > 0.
secondary: Human endgame audit (section 67 protocol, same 26 rounds, same solver budget) rerun with the new student at <= 20 cards and the champion above: critical-decision optimal rate vs humans and champion, and takeovers. Descriptive; not an acceptance metric.
evaluate.mjs descriptive exact regret on disagreements with <= 18 cards.
evaluation.notCovered: Clint or other opponents, human teammates, tribute and whole-match effects, web integration. Any web use needs a separate preregistered acceptance.

unchanged: Web champion 017 and menu, Windows campaign and all frozen runs, reward definition, GuanZero, tribute specialist, section-57 student.
